caption: The drawing depicts a section of a building featuring a window set in a thick stone wall. The window is rectangular with a wooden frame and metal grille containing a repeated scrollwork pattern. The left windowpane is closed while the right windowpane is open outward. Surrounding the window, the wall is depicted with large, pale bluish-gray stones outlined in blue, and the arch above the window is constructed of similar stones arranged radially. Below the window, the wall is divided into three horizontal bands: the uppermost is decorated with a border of blue, green, and orange geometric and floral tile patterns; the middle band is a plain ochre yellow; the lowest band is solid reddish-brown. The corner below the window creates a small ledge. The floor is illustrated with reddish-brown tiles, each with visible grid lines. Shadows are rendered to give the appearance of depth. The artwork has the names “Geoffrey Holt and Harry Mann Waddell” written in the lower right corner.
title: Restoration Drawing: Wall Painting Around Window, with Grille
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
